sec: Pre-operative blockade and intraoperative crisis · p857

items.q: The DOC α-blocker for pre-operative BP control is:
items.exp: Phenoxybenzamine (10 mg OD step-up to 10 mg TDS): non-selective, irreversible, long-lasting, non-competitive inhibitor. (Book p857)

items.q: Phenoxybenzamine is best described as a:
items.exp: It is non-selective, irreversible, long-lasting and non-competitive. (Book p857)

items.q: Other α-blockers used, and the step-up dose for prazosin, are:
opts: Prazosin (2.5 mg OD → 5 mg BD) and terazosin
items.exp: Others: prazosin (2.5 mg OD → 5 mg BD), terazosin. (Book p857)

items.q: If adequate BP control is not achieved, the added drug class is:
items.exp: Ca channel blockers amlodipine/nicardipine if adequate BP control not achieved; metyrosine rarely used. (Book p857)

items.q: HR control with β-blockers is added how many days before surgery (atenolol 12.5 mg BD → 25 mg BD)?
items.exp: 3 days before surgery: β-blockers (atenolol 12.5 mg BD → 25 mg BD) — always after α-blockade. (Book p857)

items.q: The intraoperative hypertensive crisis is managed with:
items.exp: Intraoperative hypertensive crisis: sodium nitroprusside/nicardipine. (Book p857)

items.q: Which drug is NOT part of the pre-operative preparation list?
items.exp: Metyrosine is rarely used, not first-line; phenoxybenzamine DOC, prazosin/terazosin others, atenolol for HR. (Book p857)
